----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Sanjay Nahar For Respondent(s) : Mr. Mukesh Rajpurohit, Dy.S.G.
 HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE PUSHPENDRA SINGH BHATI Order 21/07/2023 1.

This writ petition under Articles 226 & 227 of the Constitution of India has been preferred claiming the following reliefs:
"It is therefore most humbly and respectfully prayed that this writ petition filed by the petitioner may kindly be allowed and by an appropriate order or direction:
(i) The respondents be directed to consider the application for reissuance of the petitioners' passport and reissue the passport within 15 days;
(ii) Any other appropriate writ, order or direction which this Hon'ble Court may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case may kindly be passed in favour of the petitioner."

sentences.text: 1 2. Brief facts of the case, as placed before this Court by learned counsel for the petitioner, are that the respondent-authority issued [2023:RJ-JD:22898] (2 of 8) [CW-6161/2023] a passport bearing number J8682539 having its validity from 07.09.2011 to 06.09.20221.

Thereafter, in the year 2015,
an FIR bearing No.324/2015 was lodged against the petitioner for the offences under Sections 406,
420, 384, and 465 of the Indian Penal Code, at Police Station Subhash Nagar, Bhilwara and the criminal case registered in connection therewith is still pending.

2.1. After expiration of the validity period of the passport, the petitioner filed an online application, through the concerned official web portal, for re-issuance of the passport, whereupon the respondent vide letter dated 06.09.2021 sought clarification from the petitioner regarding suppression of the information relating to the aforementioned criminal proceedings against the petitioner.

Thereafter, the petitioner approached the respondent-authority to furnish the necessary explanation by bringing to the notice of respondent-authority that due to bona fide mistake, the relevant information regarding the pending criminal case was not disclosed by the petitioner.
However, despite various requests and efforts made by the petitioner, his application for re-issuance of the passport was kept pending by the respondent-authority.
Hence, the present petition has been preferred claiming the afore-quoted reliefs.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that as per law, the respondent cannot deny re-issuance of the passport to the petitioner and thus, the impugned action of the respondent is not sustainable in the eye of law.
3.1. Learned counsel further submits that the stage at which the aforementioned criminal case was pending against the petitioner, does not create any bar for re-issuance of the passport to him.

3.2. In support of his submissions, learned counsel relied upon the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu Vs Central Bureau of Investigation (Criminal Appeal No(s). 1342/2017, decided on 27.09.2021); and the judgment rendered by a Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court of Bombay in the case of Abbas Hatimbhai Kagalwala Vs The State of Maharastra & Anr. (Writ Petition No. 384 of 2019, decided on 23.08.2022).
4.

S.G. appearing on behalf of the respondents, while opposing the aforesaid submissions made on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the criminal case is still pending against the present petitioner, and therefore, the impugned action on the part of the respondent-authority is justified in law.

4.1. He further submits that the Division Bench of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the case of Abbas Hatimbhai Kagalwala (Supra) after relying upon the aforementioned judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court, clearly observed that the petitioner therein has to obtain a permission from the competent Court, where criminal case is pending, for the purpose of the issuance of the passport.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties as well as perused the record of the case alongwith the judgments cited at the Bar.
6. This Court observes that after expiration of the validity period of the earlier passport, the petitioner filed an online application for re-issuance of the passport before the respondents.

sentences.text: 7. This Court, at this juncture, considers it appropriate to reproduce the relevant portions of the judgments rendered in the cases of Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu (Supra), and Abbas Hatimbhai Kagalwala (Supra), as hereunder; Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu (Supra):

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The refusal of a passport can be only in case where an applicant is convicted during the period of 5 years immediately proceeding the date of application for an offence involving moral turpitude and sentence for imprisonment for not less than two years.
Section 6.2 (f) relates to a situation where the applicant is facing trial in a criminal court.
Admittedly, at present, the conviction of the appellant stands still the disposal of the criminal appeal.
The sentence which he has to undergo is for a period of one year.
The passport authority cannot refuse the renewal of the passport on the ground of pendency of the criminal appeal.
The passport authority is directed to renew the passport of the applicant without raising the objection relating to the pendency of the criminal appeal in this Court.
Subject to the other conditions being fulfilled, the Interlocutory Application stands disposed of."

Abbas Hatimbhai Kagalwala (Supra) :
"Learned Counsel for the Union relies upon Notification dated 25.8.1993 and Section 6.2 (f) of the Passport Act, 1967, to conclude that the Petitioner has to obtain a permission of the Court where criminal case is pending against the Petitioner for [2023:RJ-JD:22898] (6 of 8) [CW-6161/2023] the purpose of issuance of the Passport.
It will be a case of issuance of the Passport and not renewal of the Passport.
4. It is the case of the Petitioner that validity of the Passport came to an end in the year 2017.
The Petitioner applied for renewal and said application is pending for more than 4 years.
It is also a fact that a criminal case is pending against the Petitioner u/s 420, 465, 467 r/w 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

5. In view of the fact that petitioner is already issued a Passport earlier and the Petitioner would be seeking renewal of the Passport and the said application is pending with the Respondent, so also, considering the Order passed by the Apex Court in Criminal Appeal No.1342/2017 (supra) we pass the following order.
Order i) The Respondent shall process the application of the petitioner for renewal of Passport without insisting for permission of the Court, where a criminal case is pending against the Petitioner.
If the Petitioner is travelling abroad, then the Petitioner would be required to seek permission from the Court where criminal case is pending.

.... ....."

sentences.text:
10. Since the law in regard to the controversy in question has already been settled in the aforementioned precedent laws, this Court disposes of the present petition as well as all the pending [2023:RJ-JD:22898] (7 of 8) [CW-6161/2023] applications, if any, while directing the respondents to decide the application of the petitioner for renewal/reissuance of the passport, as per the following conditions:
(i) The present petitioner shall be required to submit an undertaking alongwith an affidavit before the competent Court where the criminal case in question is pending against the petitioner, stating that he shall not leave India during pendency of the said criminal case, without permission of the said Court and that he shall extend due co-operation to the said Court for conclusion of the proceedings in the criminal case.

(ii) Upon filing of such undertaking and the affidavit, the competent Court where the criminal case in question is pending against the petitioner shall issue a certified copy of the same within two weeks thereafter.

(iii) The present petitioner shall submit a certified copy of this order as well as the aforesaid undertaking and the affidavit before the concerned Passport Officer/Passport Authority for renewal/reissuance of the passport.

(iv) On submissions of the aforementioned documents, the concerned Passport Officer/Passport Authority shall consider the matter afresh, in light of the observations made hereinabove, as well as the contents of the documents, including undertaking, furnished by the petitioner for renewal/reissuance of the passport,
strictly in accordance with law within three weeks from the date of such application.

(v) Upon renewal/reissuance of the passport, the present petitioner shall deposit the original renewed/reissued passport [2023:RJ-JD:22898] (8 of 8) [CW-6161/2023]
before the competent Court where the criminal case in question is pending against the petitioner.

(vi) However, the petitioner shall be at liberty to file an application before the said competent Court seeking permission to travel abroad, and it is for the said Court to consider and decide the same, strictly in accordance with law.

(DR.PUSHPENDRA SINGH BHATI), J.
